note: A commercial ghost-tour company's write-up of the street's legends: a modern retelling of reported hauntings, cited here for what the legends say, never as evidence that anything happened. Fragments read: of Glessner House, the architect's 'spirit standing on that same staircase'; of the Kimball house, Evaline Kimball 'pounding on the windows in despair' and its big north windows that shake and rattle; of the Keith brothers, 'his ghost has been seen at his brother's house, where he sometimes appears in the windows'; of the Field Jr. house, footsteps and 'strange cries in the dead of night'; of the women's park, a woman in a settler's dress among the bushes at night, and carriage horses that 'always seem to have their bits, but never their harnesses'; of the battle park, spirits of the 1812 fallen on clear, cold nights: 'The Americans go searching for their families and friends while the Natives continue to patrol their land.'
what_it_supplies: the ghost legends told of 1800, 1801, 1900 and 1919 Prairie, the Clarke House garden and the 1812 battle ground
what_it_does_not_supply: any evidence that a haunting occurred
